en: The Aparimitāyus Sūtra:
Thus have I heard.
At one time the Blessed One was dwelling at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, in Anāthapiṇḍada’s monastery, together with a great [assembly].
Together with the community of monks consisting of twelve hundred and fifty monks, and with a great many bodhisattva mahāsattvas. // 1 //
Thereupon, the Blessed One addressed Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta:

"Mañjuśrī, above here there is a world-system named Aparimitaguṇasañcaya. Therein dwells, remains, and sustains himself a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksambuddha named Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja, for the sake of sentient beings."
And he teaches the Dharma. // 2 //
Listen, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta! These humans of Jambudvīpa have short lifespans, living for only a hundred years; many untimely deaths have been described for them.

Mañjuśrī, those beings who shall write down or cause to be written this Dharma discourse named *The Proclamation of the Qualities and Praises of the Tathāgata Aparimitāyus*, or who shall hear even its mere name, or who, having made it into a book, shall keep it in their home, recite it, and honor it with flowers, incense, perfumes, garlands, ointments, powders, robes, umbrellas, banners, bells, and flags—
They shall worship him on all sides with offerings; those whose lifespans are exhausted shall once again come to have a lifespan of one hundred years.
Furthermore, Mañjuśrī, those beings who hear, retain, or recite the one hundred and eight names of that Tathāgata Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja, their lifespans shall be increased.
For those beings whose lifespan is exhausted who hear, retain, or recite this name, their lifespan shall also increase. // 3 //

Therefore, Mañjuśrī, noble sons or noble daughters who desire long life and shall hear or write down the one hundred and eight names of that Tathāgata Aparimitāyus will possess these qualities and benefits. // 4 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One, the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Aparimitāyurjñānasuviniścitatejorāja.
It is thus:
Oṃ, merit, great merit, immeasurable merit, immeasurable life-merit, accumulated through the equipment of wisdom!
Oṃ, O nature of phenomena that is utterly pure in all conditioned things, arisen like the sky, pure by its own nature, surrounded by the Great Vehicle, svāhā! // 5 //
Mañjuśrī, those who write down these one hundred and eight names of the Tathāgata, or cause them to be written, or even having made them into a book, keep them in their home or recite them—
even those whose lifespan has been exhausted shall once again have a lifespan of a hundred years;
and passing away from here, they will be reborn in the buddha-field of the Tathāgata Aparimitāyus.
And they shall possess immeasurable lifespans in the world-system called Aparimitaguṇasañcaya. // 6 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, ninety-nine koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. // 7 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, eighty-four million Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra. (8)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, seventy-seven million Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. // 9 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, sixty-five koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and in one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra. 10.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, five hundred quintillion Buddhas, with one mind and in one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. 11.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, forty-five koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. (12)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Now at that time, thirty-six koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. (13)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, twenty-five koṭis of Buddhas, with one mind and in one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra. 14.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Furthermore, at that time, as many as ten million buddhas, equal to the sands of the river Gaṅgā, with one mind and one voice, spoke this Aparimitāyus Sūtra. (15)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Whoever shall write this Aparimitāyur-jñāna Sūtra or cause it to be written shall never be reborn in the hells, nor among the animals, nor in the world of Yama, nor ever in the inopportune states; and in whatever birth they may be reborn, [they shall be endowed with immeasurable life].
In every single birth, wherever they may be born, they will remember their past lives. // 17 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, by them eighty-four thousand aggregates of the Dharma (dharmaskandha) shall have been caused to be written. 18.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, by them eighty-four thousand stūpas for the Dharma Kings will have been caused to be built and consecrated. (19)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, their five karmic obstructions of immediate retribution shall be completely exhausted. 20.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra—for them, neither Māra, nor those belonging to Māra’s host, nor yakṣas, nor rākṣasas, nor untimely death shall find an opportunity to prevail. // 22 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, at the time of their death, ninety-nine billion Buddhas will grant them a vision of themselves face to face.
A thousand Buddhas will place their hands one upon the other for him as he travels from Buddha-field to Buddha-field;
in this regard, no doubt, no uncertainty, and no hesitation should be conceived. 23.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, for that person the Four Great Kings shall follow closely behind and provide protection, defense, and guardianship. // 24 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra will be reborn in the world-system Sukhāvatī, the Buddha-field of the Tathāgata Amitābha. 25.
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write this Aparimitāyus Sūtra or cause it to be written, that spot of earth shall become like a shrine (caitya) and worthy of veneration.
Those animals and birds belonging to the animal realm into whose ears it shall fall will all fully awaken to unsurpassed, perfect enlightenment. // 26 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall write or cause to be written this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, for that person there shall never again be the state of being a woman. (27)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Whoever, with reference to this Aparimitāyus Sūtra, this discourse on Dharma, shall give even a single kārṣāpaṇa as a gift, by that person a gift equal to filling the triple-thousand great-thousand world-system with the seven precious jewels will have been given. (28)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Whoever shall worship this Dharma-preacher has thereby worshipped the true Dharma in its entirety and completion. // 29 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Just as it might be possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit from having performed offerings consisting of the seven precious gems to the Tathāgatas, such as Vipaśyin, Śikhin, Viśvabhū, Krakucchanda, Kanakamuni, Kāśyapa, and Śākyamuni;
But it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit of this *Aparimitāyus-sūtra*. // 30 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

It may be possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit for one who were to give a gift by making a heap of jewels equal in size to Sumeru, the king of mountains; but [it is not possible to calculate the merit of this other].
But it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit of the *Aparimitāyus Sūtra*. // 31 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
Just as the four great oceans might be filled with water, it would be possible to count each individual drop therein; [but not so the merit of this].
But it is not possible to calculate the measure of the mass of merit of this *Aparimitāyus* Sūtra. // 32 //
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Whoever shall write this Aparimitāyur-jñāna-sūtra, or cause it to be written, and having prepared it, shall honor it, by that person all the Tathāgatas in all the Buddha-fields throughout the ten directions will have been saluted and honored. (33)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!
The Buddha has arisen through the power of generosity; the Lion among Men has attained the power of generosity.
And the sound of the power of generosity is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. (34)

The Buddha has arisen through the power of ethical discipline; the Lion among Men has attained the power of ethical discipline. And the sound of that compassionate one’s power of ethical discipline is heard as he enters the city. (35)
The Buddha has arisen through the power of patience; the Lion among Men has attained the power of patience.
And the sound of the power of patience is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. (36)
The Buddha has arisen through the power of vigor; the Lion among Men has attained it by the power of vigor.
And the sound of the power of vigor is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. (37)
The Buddha has arisen by the power of meditative concentration; the Lion among Men has attained the power of meditative concentration.
And the sound of the compassionate one’s power of meditative concentration is heard as he enters the city. (38)
The Buddha has arisen through the power of wisdom; the lion among men has attained the power of wisdom.
And the sound of the power of wisdom is heard as the Compassionate One enters the city. (39)
Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One!

Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the monks, those bodhisattva mahāsattvas, and the entire assembly—including the world of gods, humans, asuras, and gandharvas—rejoiced and highly praised what the Blessed One had spoken. (40)
